Let's try the other way around as well: If I make a great platforming game but after an update, you have to play an idle game for a while to get an ascension in order to play another platforming level, will this make the game bad?
If I make an idle game but after a game update, you have to do a great platforming level every time you do ascension to get prestige, will this make the game bad?

One way or the other, it will be frustrating to the players who would normally play the respective kind of game.

A platform-game is expected to be at least moderately fast and all about speed of reaction and precision of timing, estimates of trajectory etc. In short, it is meant to be engaging and require enough skills to be a challenge to advanced players.

The "idle game" in comparison is entirely different. To avoid going to extremes, let's consider something that still takes some skill, like Patience. It engages logics and has you make reasonable assumptions on which cards are still in the deck and how you can possibly order them correctly.

One has you longing for more action as long as you keep playing, the other one is really quite calm. Even if both sequences are well made, they will break the "flow" of each other and if you force that on a player, your game will be a very niche product at least.

EDIT: Also, consider when and where those games are generally played. An office worker who uses an idle-game to keep the mind occupied while doing some repetitive task will likely not be able to completely interrupt the work and play an action game.
